source.title: Towards Architectural-Level Safety Control: Relocating Hazardous Knowledge into Removable Experts in Mixture-of-Experts Models
source.authors: Cheng Jin; Zhong-Tian Ma; Xiao Wang; Han Qi; Xiaoyu Wen; Xiang Wang; You-Bang Sun; Xia Hu; Bo-Wen Zhou; Chao-Chao Lu; Qiao-Sheng Zhang

page_placements.theme: Unlearning recovery and resistance depend on method

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses shallow alignment and unlearning, but its experiments measure hazardous-knowledge benchmark accuracy in MoE models, not refusal behavior, response-position KL, or bypasses of refusal.
record.gate_note: The paper reports WMDP accuracy and capability separation. These are related to hazardous knowledge but do not measure the user-directed harmful compliance or safety behavior named in V1–V7; the WMDP results are recorded as findings fitting no version. The paper's cited claims about ordinary fine-tuning restoring unlearned knowledge are not its own results.
record.test_reason: The paper measures hazardous-knowledge accuracy on WMDP multiple-choice, without a chat template, in MoE models after expert excision and standard SFT. It never measures refusal or harmful-request compliance, per-token KL by response position, prefill or suffix bypasses, or safety-behaviour localization. Shallow alignment (Qi et al. 2025a) appears only as motivation in the introduction and in Figure 1's framing.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that REX relocates hazardous knowledge into removable MoE experts, matches the strongest of nine unlearning baselines on base-model WMDP, and is the only method whose removal largely survives standard fine-tuning. General capability is preserved and keeps improving. They frame release as an architectural choice, contrasting this with behavioural alignment, which they call shallow, and with in-place unlearning.
record.recipe_differences: The study expands pretrained MoE models with target experts, relocates hazardous-domain knowledge, excises those experts, and measures WMDP accuracy. It does not use the refusal, token-position KL, or bypass methods in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by backbone and target domain; the paper reports weaker excision reductions for Gemma 4 / Cyber than for several other settings. Standard post-training outcomes also differ by model, domain, and unlearning route.

fits_no_version.finding: Excising the REX target experts lowers WMDP accuracy by 9.5–48.4 points at the base stage and 11.1–38.9 points after SFT, across three MoE backbones and two domains. The median general-capability change is 0.6 points.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hazardous-domain benchmark knowledge can be relocated into removable MoE experts and excised with little general-capability loss.

fits_no_version.finding: Standard 250M-token SFT on a benign instruction mix (life-science subsets removed) restores much of the WMDP accuracy removed by parameter-level unlearning. For example, RMU on Qwen3.5/Bio goes from 44.1 to 78.3. REX's delivered model rises less (32.4 to 42.8). This is knowledge recovery, not compliance, so it is only an analogue of V2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign fine-tuning restores unlearned hazardous knowledge stored in shared parameters; structural excision bounds this rebound.

fits_no_version.finding: In a random-expert excision control on Intern-S2/Bio (Table 11), WMDP stays at 78.9±0.9 against 79.4 for the full model. Excising the target experts gives 64.3. Not recorded as a row; declared in rows_left_out only implicitly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The drop in hazardous knowledge is specific to the relocated experts, not to removing any parameters of equal size.

record.problems: The study does not measure refusal or harmful-request compliance, and WMDP accuracy is not a direct measure of those behaviors. The text reports a five-seed random-expert excision control with seed-level standard deviations, but most tabulated comparisons provide no uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2's full set of unlearning-baseline endpoint scores, Table 4's relocation ablations, Table 5's pipeline ablations, and routing-mass diagnostics are not included. They are additional results on WMDP, general benchmarks, or routing measurements rather than the claim's named refusal, token-position, or bypass outcomes; the included Table 1 and Table 3 rows capture the direct excision and SFT benchmark results.

untested.parts: Fine-tuning on harmful examples and the resulting harmful-request compliance; no harmful-example fine-tuning is run.
Benign fine-tuning effect on refusal or harmful compliance. The 250M-token SFT on a benign instruction mix is measured only by WMDP knowledge accuracy.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models across response positions.
Prefilling, adversarial suffixes or decoding changes as refusal bypasses.
Localization of safety (refusal) behaviour in few weights or ranks. The paper localizes hazardous knowledge into experts it adds itself, which is a different construct.
Whether data or the training objective causes shallow safety.
Training that deepens refusal beyond the first tokens, and its durability.

record.verdict_notes: Relation could arguably be cites_only: the shallow-alignment paper is cited once in the introduction as motivation and is not engaged further. All 47 rows are correctly linked to none. WMDP is a 0-shot multiple-choice knowledge test run without a chat template, so it cannot show refusal or compliance. The reader's per-row states (partial/observed) describe the size of changes in WMDP accuracy, not any claim version.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful-example fine-tuning and refusal or harmful-request compliance.
Benign-data fine-tuning effects on refusal or harmful-request compliance.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes as refusal bypasses.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior; the paper measures removable-expert effects on WMDP accuracy instead.
Whether data or training objectives cause safety behavior to be shallow.
Training that deepens safety behavior beyond early response tokens and its durability.

relation.reason: The introduction and discussion contrast REX with shallow behavioral alignment; the experiments neither test nor use the claimed safety-alignment effects.

tranche.reason: The experiments measure hazardous-knowledge removal and recovery using WMDP accuracy, a related construct that does not test any listed claim version.

source_check.notes: All listed numerical pairs match Table 3. Standard SFT uses a text-only instruction mixture with life-science subsets removed; WMDP is a four-way knowledge test, not harmful-request compliance.
